title: Gladness Was Spread Through Israel's Host
description: Gladness Was Spread Through Israel's Host in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 49, “A famine of the word”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Glad-ness was spread through Is-rael's host When first they Man-na viewed; They la-bored who should ga-ther most, And thought it plea-sant food.

lines: Gladness was spread through Israel's host
They labored who should gather most,
But when they had it long enjoyed
From day to day, the same;
Their hearts were by the plenty cloyed,
Thus gospel bread at first is prized,
But should the Lord, displeased, withhold
To have our houses filled with gold
How tedious would the week appear,
Could we no longer meet to bear
The gospel, and a praying few
But Olney sure the day will rue
Then sin, in this once favored town,
And wrath and vengeance hasten down,
Preserve us from this judgment, Lord
A famine of the gospel word

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
